title: Emmeline Pankhurst
summary: Emmeline Pankhurst (1858–1928) was a British political activist who led the militant campaign for women's suffrage in the United Kingdom. In 1903, she founded the Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU), adopting direct action and civil disobedience under the slogan 'deeds, not words.' Her leadership propelled women's enfranchisement to the forefront of national politics, contributing decisively to the passage of voting rights legislation for British women in 1918 and full equal franchise shortly after her death in 1928.

uncertainty.note: Born July 1858 (birth registered 15 July 1858; family celebrated 14 July 1858); died 14 June 1928.
